project.name: VentuSample
project.focus: Deterministic sample generation, bounded offline DSP, PCM16 WAV export, and versioned sample-pack manifests.

principles: Pull-request review and required checks for source changes
Observable failures and explicit recovery ceilings
Human approval for external or destructive operations

phases.name: Phase 1 — Baseline and contract
exit_criteria: The JSON roadmap, schema, documentation, evidence paths, and safety settings pass the contract workflow.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Continuous verification
exit_criteria: Existing CI, architecture, quality, synchronization, and auto-merge checks remain authoritative.
New diagnostics are read-only, bounded, and observable.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Recovery, scale, and release gates
exit_criteria: Recovery and scaling are tested for idempotence and resource bounds.
Deployment and publication remain disabled until an approved target, rollback plan, and protected environment exist.

tasks.objective: Version and validate one machine-readable automation roadmap for this repository.
tasks.target: Plan changes through reviewed roadmap updates and contract checks.
guardrails: Roadmap changes are reviewed as versioned source.
Do not represent planned work as implemented.
tasks.acceptance: The roadmap contract is valid, identifies all 20 workstreams, and its evidence paths exist.

tasks.objective: Use event-driven CI and scheduled read-only checks with explicit manual dispatch.
tasks.target: Run only on declared push, pull-request, schedule, or manual events.
guardrails: Scheduled checks are read-only.
No workflow receives write permissions by default.
tasks.acceptance: Eligible workflows start from their declared triggers and use least-privilege permissions.

tasks.objective: Keep project contracts and peer-integration metadata synchronized with repository reality.
tasks.target: Validate declared contracts and only synchronize eligible same-repository pull requests.
guardrails: Never overwrite a changed branch head.
Keep interface versions explicit.
tasks.acceptance: Contract and federation metadata validate without silently changing runtime behavior.

tasks.objective: Make improvement intake traceable by impact, risk, dependencies, and verification cost.
tasks.target: Use conflict and remediation records; require review for priority changes.
guardrails: Priority changes require rationale and maintainer review.
Do not suppress competing findings.
tasks.acceptance: Each proposed improvement has a priority, rationale, acceptance condition, and evidence.

tasks.objective: Keep project metadata, configuration contracts, and generated inventories current.
tasks.target: Regenerate only deterministic metadata; validate before acceptance.
guardrails: Only deterministic configuration may be generated.
Never commit environment-specific secrets.
tasks.acceptance: Declared configuration matches the current repository and validates against its contract.

tasks.objective: Tune build and toolchain configuration from measured evidence rather than speculative changes.
tasks.target: Benchmark before changing defaults; keep platform-specific overrides explicit.
guardrails: Do not trade correctness for speed.
Keep measured baselines and regression tests.
tasks.acceptance: Any optimization includes a reproducible baseline and a regression check.

tasks.objective: Keep eligible pull-request branches current with main without overwriting concurrent work.
tasks.target: Check repository ownership, target branch, draft state, and expected head SHA.
guardrails: Same-repository, non-draft PRs targeting main only.
Use expected-head SHA and leave conflicts unresolved.
tasks.acceptance: Only eligible, unchanged, same-repository branches are updated; conflicts are left for review.

tasks.objective: Validate cross-project interfaces and shared federation metadata as versioned contracts.
tasks.target: Require explicit interface versions and local evidence for each integration.
guardrails: Validate declared interfaces before integration.
No hidden network or central runtime dependency.
tasks.acceptance: Peer links and interface declarations validate without introducing a central runtime dependency.

tasks.objective: Route defects through root-cause remediation, regression coverage, and verified integration.
tasks.target: Automated checks may diagnose and validate; code fixes remain reviewable changes.
guardrails: Automated remediation proposes verifiable changes; no blind rewrites.
Preserve regression evidence.
tasks.acceptance: Every accepted correction has a reproducible regression test and passing verification.

tasks.objective: Run repeatable diagnostics on repository events and scheduled maintenance checks.
tasks.target: Keep diagnostic jobs read-only unless a narrowly scoped write is explicitly required.
guardrails: Diagnostics are read-only.
Do not execute code discovered from untrusted PRs in privileged contexts.
tasks.acceptance: Diagnostics produce actionable failures and do not mutate source or production systems.

tasks.objective: Organize validation into focused test suites with deterministic update checks.
tasks.target: Run focused tests for changed contracts and the full required suite before merge.
guardrails: Required test suites remain merge gates.
Do not auto-delete or weaken tests.
tasks.acceptance: Test groups are repeatable, failures are visible, and updates cannot bypass required checks.

tasks.objective: Scale validation through bounded matrices, parallel jobs, and resource-aware test selection.
tasks.target: Cap concurrency and runtime; measure before raising matrix size.
guardrails: Bound matrix size, runtime, and concurrency.
Retain all required platform checks.
tasks.acceptance: Expanded validation stays within declared time and resource budgets without reducing required coverage.

tasks.objective: Verify architecture, quality, and compatibility contracts as executable acceptance gates.
tasks.target: Treat missing evidence as a failure, not as an inferred success.
guardrails: Missing evidence fails closed.
Never bypass branch protection or required checks.
tasks.acceptance: Acceptance gates check current evidence and report the exact failing contract.

tasks.objective: Define environment-aware deployment and scaling only where the repository has a real deployable target.
tasks.target: Require protected environments and an explicit human approval before external deployment.
guardrails: External deployment requires a protected environment and human approval.
No production rollout is enabled by this roadmap.
tasks.acceptance: A deployment workflow is added only with a documented target, rollback path, permissions, and approval gate.

tasks.objective: Consolidate duplicate checks and maintain a coherent native and cross-platform verification matrix.
tasks.target: Do not remove a check unless equivalent coverage is demonstrated.
guardrails: Remove duplicate checks only after equivalent coverage is proven.
Keep platform-specific tests.
tasks.acceptance: The consolidated matrix preserves platform coverage and publishes unambiguous results.

tasks.objective: Add bounded recovery for transient CI and artifact failures with explicit retry ceilings.
tasks.target: Never retry destructive actions or conceal a persistent failure as success.
guardrails: Retries are idempotent and capped.
Persistent failures remain failures and are surfaced.
tasks.acceptance: Recovery is idempotent, capped, observable, and followed by the same verification gates.

tasks.objective: Test safety boundaries, invalid inputs, failure paths, and diagnostic reporting.
tasks.target: Prefer isolated fixtures; never run hardware-changing operations in CI.
guardrails: Use isolated fixtures and test hardware boundaries safely.
Do not flash firmware or install drivers in CI.
tasks.acceptance: Regression tests cover normal, boundary, invalid, and failure cases for the repository's core path.

tasks.objective: Make workflow health, failed checks, stale branches, and recovery outcomes observable.
tasks.target: Report only sourced workflow and repository state; do not auto-dismiss failures.
guardrails: Preserve failed-run and merge-block evidence.
Do not auto-dismiss alerts or failures.
tasks.acceptance: A maintainer can trace each validation, synchronization, retry, and merge decision.

tasks.objective: Keep automation design, evidence, limits, and maintenance ownership documented alongside code.
tasks.target: Generate only deterministic documentation; preserve human review for semantic changes.
guardrails: Generated documentation is deterministic and reviewable.
Do not overwrite hand-maintained project guidance.
tasks.acceptance: Documentation lists all workstreams, current status, evidence, safety limits, and next acceptance gates.

tasks.objective: Prepare reproducible release packaging and publication after release criteria are explicitly defined.
tasks.target: No unattended publication, signing, firmware installation, or production release.
guardrails: Publishing requires a protected release ref and explicit approval.
No unattended signing, external publication, or deployment.
tasks.acceptance: Publication runs only from a protected release ref with verified artifacts and an approved release gate.
